recent_posts.title: Teradata launches platform for enterprise AI agents moving beyond pilots
recent_posts.summary: Teradata has launched its Autonomous Knowledge Platform, consolidating data, analytics, AI development, agent orchestration, and governance into a single offering for enterprises. The platform targets companies moving AI agents from pilot to production, addressing key concerns around data access controls, cost management, and accountability. Key components include AI Studio, the Tera natural-language workspace, Tera Agents for infrastructure operations (sizing, tuning, FinOps), Elastic Compute on Teradata Cloud, and the upcoming Teradata Factory for on-premises workloads. A central governance layer called Enterprise MCP enforces authentication, role-based access, schema validation, and audit trails for every agent tool call. Analysts describe it as a strategic consolidation rather than a clean-sheet invention, noting that the prebuilt infrastructure-focused Tera Agents may be the most differentiated element. The platform enters a competitive market alongside Snowflake, Databricks, Microsoft, Oracle, and Salesforce. Availability on Teradata Cloud is planned for Q3, with multi-agent orchestration entering research preview by year-end.

recent_posts.title: Three skills that matter when AI handles the coding
recent_posts.summary: As AI tools like Claude Code and Cursor take over code generation, developers must shift focus to three upstream skills: writing effective prompts with rich context, critically evaluating AI-generated code, and retaining deep coding knowledge to avoid 'cognitive debt.' Good prompts require solid requirements analysis, architecture understanding, and system design. The piece warns against over-reliance on LLMs, noting that hallucinations and confidently wrong outputs are real risks. Drawing on Fred Brooks' 'No Silver Bullet,' it argues AI can reduce accidental complexity but cannot eliminate essential complexity inherent to software problems. Developers who master higher-level design thinking alongside AI tooling will significantly outperform those who don't.

recent_posts.title: MongoDB targets AI’s retrieval problem
recent_posts.summary: MongoDB is releasing a suite of AI-focused features to address the retrieval and memory problems that undermine trust in LLM-powered agents. Key announcements include Automated Voyage AI Embeddings in MongoDB Vector Search (public preview), general availability of a LangGraph.js Long-Term Memory Store for JavaScript/TypeScript developers, and native integration of embedding and re-ranking models from the Voyage AI acquisition. MongoDB 8.3 is also generally available, featuring architectural improvements for faster AI workloads. Additional updates include an Atlas integration with the Feast open-source feature store and cross-region AWS PrivateLink connectivity for security and compliance. The overarching goal is to consolidate fragmented AI stacks into a single platform, eliminating complex data pipelines and reducing what MongoDB calls the 'synchronization tax.'

recent_posts.title: Building AI apps and agents with Microsoft Foundry
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft Foundry is a unified Azure-based platform for building, deploying, and governing AI agents and models. It consolidates previous Azure AI services into a single platform serving three audiences: application developers, ML engineers/data scientists, and IT administrators. Key features include multi-agent orchestration, a model catalog with models from Microsoft and partners like Anthropic and Meta, a tool catalog, guardrails for responsible AI, and observability via OpenTelemetry. Developers can work in Python, C#, TypeScript/JavaScript, or Java, with 18 solution templates available. The platform supports prompt agents, workflow agents, and hosted agents, and integrates with LangChain/LangGraph, MCP, and Claude Code. A hands-on test of the 'Get started with AI agents' template cost $0.02 and took about an hour. The reviewer rated Foundry favorably, comparable to Google ADK and better than Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, praising the Agents Playground and model selection while noting the documentation can be overwhelming.

recent_posts.title: Designing front-end systems for cloud failure
recent_posts.summary: Frontend applications depend on cloud services for authentication, search, analytics, and more — making frontend reliability tightly coupled to cloud reliability. Rather than treating failures as total outages, engineers should design for partial degradation: isolating failures by component, separating critical from non-critical features, using controlled retries with exponential backoff and jitter, preserving user input during failed submissions, and rendering partial content when some dependencies are unavailable. Clear, specific error messages that explain what failed and what still works are emphasized over generic fallback text. Tools like the Fetch API and AbortController help manage request lifecycles cleanly. The core mindset shift is designing interfaces for real operating conditions rather than perfect demos.

recent_posts.title: Oracle will patch more often to counter AI cybersecurity threat
recent_posts.summary: Oracle is shifting from quarterly to monthly security patch releases, introducing Critical Security Patch Updates (CSPUs) starting May 28, 2026. The change is driven by the accelerating pace of AI-enabled vulnerability discovery. Oracle will release patches on the third Tuesday of each month, a week after Microsoft, SAP, and Adobe. The company is leveraging OpenAI and Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview to identify and fix vulnerabilities faster. Quarterly cumulative Critical Patch Updates will continue alongside the new monthly cadence. On-premises and third-party hosted customers will need to apply patches manually, while Oracle-managed cloud customers receive automatic updates.

recent_posts.title: The agentic AI distraction
recent_posts.summary: Cloud providers are over-investing in agentic AI while neglecting foundational infrastructure problems like outages, platform fragmentation, and operational complexity. The argument is that agentic AI requires mature, stable infrastructure to deliver real value, but many providers haven't yet earned that maturity. Enterprises care more about uptime, simplicity, and reliability than flashy AI agent demos. The recommendation is for providers to treat resilience and platform coherence as strategic priorities rather than maintenance, and to position agentic AI as a complement to — not a substitute for — solid fundamentals.

recent_posts.title: Diskless databases: What happens when storage isn’t the bottleneck
recent_posts.summary: Diskless database architectures separate compute from storage, replacing local disk persistence with in-memory indexing backed by object storage. This eliminates the storage bottleneck common in high-throughput workloads like telemetry, IoT, and industrial AI systems. Benefits include independent scaling of compute and storage, automatic fault isolation, multi-AZ durability without complex replication, and zero-downtime upgrades. The shift enables real-time ingestion and querying at petabyte scale, allowing predictive maintenance, industrial control, and ML systems to operate on live data streams rather than batched snapshots.

recent_posts.title: SAP to acquire data lakehouse vendor Dremio
recent_posts.summary: SAP has announced plans to acquire Dremio, an agentic lakehouse company, for an undisclosed price. The key differentiator driving the deal is Dremio's ability to query and federate enterprise data in place — without requiring data movement or format conversion — using Apache Iceberg as an open table format foundation. This addresses a critical gap for SAP's enterprise customers, whose data landscapes are typically fragmented across legacy warehouses, departmental lakes, and on-prem systems. Analysts note that acquiring Snowflake or Databricks was never realistic due to cost and neutrality concerns, as Dremio lets SAP sit above the warehouse layer and interoperate with both platforms. The acquisition is also seen as correcting SAP's earlier failure to develop native Apache Iceberg capabilities. Analysts advise CIOs with active Snowflake/Databricks contracts to watch for SAP steering new AI workloads toward Business Data Cloud by 2027.

recent_posts.title: Making AI work through eval hygiene
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic shipped three quality regressions in Claude Code over six weeks that its own evals failed to catch — a wake-up call for any team deploying AI in production. The core argument is that most AI teams have a measurement problem, not a quality problem. Good evals aren't just test suites; they encode what quality means for a specific product, separate regression from capability testing, and treat user complaints as the most valuable input. Practical guidance includes: writing 20–50 evals drawn from real production failures, distinguishing pass@k from pass^k for reliability requirements, separating quality/latency/cost as independent trade-offs, making regression scores a hard release gate rather than a report, and writing the eval before writing the prompt. Bad evals — too narrow, uncalibrated LLM-as-judge, never updated — create false confidence that is worse than no measurement at all.
